inferred_rule: The roster comes first, then every template is filed against it. You are not sorting templates by shape, you are choosing a fixed cast of about fifteen standing agents that mirror the roles in the operation you actually run, and then asking of each file: is this file the best embodiment of one of those roles (Template), is its work a kind of work that belongs on a role that already has a seat (Recipe, and you name the seat in the agent column even when that seat has no Template yet), or does no seat want it (Delete). Three consequences follow that the shape-based reading misses. First, at most one file per role gets Template, which is why only five exist against about fourteen named seats: the other seats will be assembled out of Recipe-flagged responsibilities rather than inherited from a file. Second, Recipe does not mean the template was one workflow, it means the template dissolves and its content survives as one or more responsibilities on a named owner. Third, within every cluster of templates doing the same job, exactly one is chosen as the carrier and the rest are deleted regardless of individual quality, which is why the Delete list is full of perfectly good templates.
rule_strains_where: Security Sentinel (Template) declares exactly ONE use case, which is a single workflow. Under the stated rule in _director_findings section 13 it should be a Recipe. It survives because the ROLE has several latent kinds of work (dependency CVEs, secrets, risky patterns, plus the pen tests your annotation adds) even though the file packs them into one recipe. The criterion is the role's latent decomposition, not the file's declared capability count.

Digital Clone (Template) and Idea Harvester (Template) both decompose into STAGES of one pipeline (triage then draft then digest; harvest then triage then analyze), which is exactly what the stated rule says makes a Recipe. They survive because each is the carrier for a whole class of work that other templates then fold into: six templates route into Harvester, two into Digital Clone.

Financial Stocks Signaller (Recipe) has three responsibilities in your own annotation (periodic digests, gem discovery, congressional disclosure) that are unambiguously KINDS of work, not stages. Under the stated rule it should be a Template. It is a Recipe because the Investor seat does not exist as a file yet, so the content waits as a responsibility. This is the clearest evidence that Template versus Recipe is about which file becomes the seat, not about internal structure.

QA Guardian and Content Performance Reporter carry your own 'Responsibility per type of X' phrasing, the same phrasing that justified keeping DevOps Guardian and Security Sentinel as Templates, and yet both are Recipes. The difference is that App Master and Harvester already have carriers.

Router (Template) has two capabilities and one of them is configuration, not work. It survives for a reason none of the other four share: it is the universal event door that the rest of the roster needs, so it is infrastructure rather than a role with several kinds of work.
delete_logic: Delete is not 'not a role'. It resolves into three distinct reasons, and separating them matters because they have different reversibility. (1) REDUNDANT WITH A CHOSEN CARRIER, the largest group. You say it out loud four times ('Consolidate into Technical decision tracker responsibilities' for knowledge-base-review-cycle-manager, ai-document-intelligence-hub and self-evolving-codebase-memory; 'Consolidate into survey responsibility above' for survey-processor) and apply it silently many more times: codebase-health-scanner against lean-codebase-sentinel, security-vulnerability-pipeline against security-sentinel, docs-steward against the Librarian, market-intelligence-scout and linkedin-watchlist-scout and ai-weekly-research and ai-research-report-generator against product-scout. Note that consolidation can land as EITHER verdict: product-scout is a Recipe with a consolidate note because it brought new responsibilities to the Harvester, while knowledge-base-review-cycle-manager is a Delete because it brought nothing the carrier lacked. The test is whether the file adds a kind of work, not whether it overlaps. (2) OUTSIDE THE OPERATION YOU RUN. recruiting-pipeline-use-case, sheets-e-commerce-command-center, freelancer-invoice-autopilot, user-lifecycle-manager, customer-feedback-router, youtube-content-pipeline, game-character-animator, personal-finance-use-case, brand-protection-sentinel, plus the enterprise SDLC ceremony set (design-handoff-coordinator, dev-lifecycle-manager, feature-flag-experiment-analyst, feature-flag-governance-use-case, build-intelligence-use-case, deadline-synchronizer). These are for a business with clients, staff, a sales team or a release board, none of which is present. (3) A UNIVERSAL STEP RATHER THAN A SEPARABLE RESPONSIBILITY, which you name explicitly once: code-reviewer, 'Should be part of any development process'. That reason is worth keeping distinct because it deletes work you obviously DO want, on the grounds that it belongs inside every workflow rather than to any one agent. A corroborating signal that is strong but not decisive: almost every Delete is anchored to a SaaS you do not run (Zendesk, HubSpot, Salesforce, Calendly, Stripe, Xero, Confluence, Canva, Buffer) while almost every Recipe rests on things you do have (a codebase, email, a database, the web, a vault, Claude itself). It is not decisive because autonomous-issue-resolver is Jira-anchored and you kept it as a Recipe, reframing it as 'Responsibility per issue resource to track' and generalizing away from the vendor. So the job decides, and the connector only predicts.
